references.text: The penalty for neglecting Passover is to be cut off from Israel, the same consequence as eating leavened bread during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
The Passover regulation applies to all who live among the people of Israel, and no uncircumcised person may eat of it.
The expression 'cut off from his people' is also used for one who refuses circumcision, showing the seriousness of breaking God's covenant.
Being cut off from the people is the penalty for eating a peace offering in uncleanness, parallel to neglecting the Passover sacrifice.
Anyone who does not bring their offering to the tabernacle shall be cut off, following the same principle as failing to offer the Passover sacrifice.
Approaching holy things in uncleanness leads to being cut off, emphasizing the importance of purity in sacrifices.
Whoever sins deliberately shall be cut off from the people and bear their guilt, using the same wording found in this verse.
Anyone who does not cleanse themselves after becoming unclean shall be cut off from Israel because they have defiled the Lord's sanctuary.
In the New Testament there is a warning about serious consequences for those who deliberately reject God's grace and treat Christ's blood with contempt.
